description: Sayadieh is a classic Middle Eastern seafood dish featuring fragrant spiced rice topped with perfectly cooked fish and rich caramelized onions. This comforting and flavorful meal is a staple in many coastal regions, offering a delightful blend of savory and aromatic notes. It's a truly satisfying dish that brings the taste of the Mediterranean to your table.

cumin, coriander, allspice, cinnamon, black pepper

instructions.title: Prepare the Caramelized Onions
instructions.text: Heat 1/4 cup of olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the thinly sliced onions and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until they are deeply golden brown and caramelized. This slow cooking is key to developing their sweet, rich flavor. Remove about half of the caramelized onions and set aside for garnish.

instructions.title: Create the Sayadieh Base
instructions.text: To the pot with the remaining caramelized onions, add the Sayadieh spice mix and stir for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the rinsed and drained basmati rice to the pot and stir gently to coat the grains with the spices and onion flavor. Cook for 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Cook the Rice
instructions.text: Pour in the fish stock or water and add salt. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during this process. Once cooked, let the rice rest, covered, for another 5 minutes off the heat.

instructions.title: Prepare and Cook the Fish
instructions.text: While the rice is cooking, pat the fish fillets dry and season them lightly with salt and a pinch of Sayadieh spice mix. In a separate large skillet, heat the remaining 1/4 cup of olive oil over medium-high heat. Carefully place the fish fillets in the hot oil and sear for 3-4 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until cooked through and lightly golden. Be careful not to overcook.

instructions.title: Toast Pine Nuts (Optional)
instructions.text: In a small dry pan, toast the pine nuts over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden brown. Watch them closely as they can burn quickly. Set aside.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve
instructions.text: Fluff the cooked Sayadieh rice with a fork. To serve, spoon a generous portion of the fragrant rice onto a serving platter. Gently place the seared fish fillets on top of the rice. Garnish with the reserved caramelized onions, toasted pine nuts, and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side for a fresh squeeze.

tips: For the best caramelization, cook onions slowly over medium-low heat. This allows their natural sugars to develop without burning, creating a deep, sweet flavor that is crucial for Sayadieh.
Use a firm white fish that holds its shape well, such as cod, snapper, or seabass. Avoid flaky fish that might disintegrate into the rice. Freshness is key for seafood dishes.
Toasting pine nuts enhances their nutty flavor and adds a delightful crunch. Make sure to watch them carefully as they can burn quickly; a light golden color is perfect.
